title: Can QE close the gap?

readouts.v: {abs(Y-1000)<0.05 ? "none" : (Y<1000 ? "negative output gap of " : "positive output gap of ") + fmt(abs(Y-1000),1)}

predict.q: Real output **950**; full-employment output **1000**; policy rate already near zero. The central bank buys **200** of bonds, but households and firms are very gloomy and banks are reluctant to lend. What happens?

options.s: Real output rises all the way to 1000
options.fb: That needs confidence and lending to respond fully. With gloomy borrowers, much of the new money sits idle.

options.s: Real output rises a little; most of the gap remains
options.fb: With low confidence 200 of QE lifts output only to about 963: most of the gap of 50 remains.

options.s: Only the price level rises; real output stays at 950
options.fb: There is spare capacity, so a rise in AD raises real output, not just prices.

options.s: Nothing happens to AD, because QE only changes bond prices
options.fb: Lower yields and higher asset prices do feed into spending, but weakly when confidence is low.

task: Set confidence to low and move the QE slider; then set confidence to high and repeat.

target.do: Set QE to 200 with low confidence, then press Check.

takeaway: With low confidence, 200 of QE lifts output only to about 963; with high confidence, 200 closes the gap, and 400 overshoots to 1050, with the price level up to 115.
